page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.39-156 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor. The instance features 39 dedicated physical cores running at a 3.9 GHz clock speed. With two threads per core enabled, it delivers 78 vCPUs coupled with 156 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio.

This server profile includes zero dedicated GPUs and contains no bundled local storage, requiring attached network block volumes for persistent data storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The primary architectural tradeoff is the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, which prioritizes core density and high compute frequency over extensive per-core RAM capacity.

By maximizing CPU capacity without provisioning excess memory, the instance delivers high compute resource density for processing-dominated tasks. The configuration is appropriate for compute-bound workloads including software compilation pipelines, distributed batch jobs, digital signal or media rendering, and concurrent application services that do not require massive in-memory datasets.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.39-156 is a compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at 3.9 GHz, it provisions 39 dedicated physical cores supporting 78 vCPUs via multithreading, alongside 156 GB of system memory for a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance features no bundled local disk storage and zero GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage for persistence. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Designed to offer high instruction throughput per compute allocation, this configuration trades expansive memory capacity for dense parallel processing capability. VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.39-156 is suitable for CPU-heavy deployments including distributed batch computing, build automation, scientific simulations, and scalable web application servers.
